title: Improve Dedicated Autoscaler: throughput guarantees, burst controls, and utilization reporting
author: Marina Lopez
description: Motivation: customers on Dedicated require predictable throughput SLAs while still supporting short bursts of traffic. This PR implements token-bucket based burst controls for the dedicated autoscaler, adds explicit throughput-guarantee configuration at the fleet level, and extends utilization reporting so SRE and billing can reason about reserved vs burst consumption. The changes are backwards-compatible: default configs mirror current behavior and opt-in fields enable guarantees and smoothing. Summary of changes: 1) Autoscaler: new token-bucket burst controller, smoothing window, and priority-aware token refill for multi-tenant fleets. 2) Throughput guarantees: fleet-level config fields (min_rps_per_capacity, guaranteed_tokens_per_minute) and admission checks that ensure committed capacity can be met. 3) Reporting: added metrics exported to the console and observability pipeline: dedicated.fleet.guaranteed_capacity, dedicated.fleet.burst_consumption, dedicated.fleet.token_saturation, dedicated.fleet.effective_throughput. 4) API/Console: new UI controls for setting guarantees and burst smoothing; RBAC gating for changing guarantees. 5) Tests & migration: comprehensive unit and integration tests, migration path that preserves existing autoscaler configs. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-4321) - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests with canary cluster - [x] console UI changes behind feature flag - [x] backwards compatibility validation - [x] observability dashboards updated Notes: this PR touches both runtime autoscaler and control-plane reporting paths. The token-bucket algorithm is implemented in autoscaler/core/token_bucket_controller.go and exercised with a synthetic workload harness. The admission check prevents enabling a throughput guarantee if committed capacity is insufficient; operators can run a dry-run report to see required capacity before applying. See related PRs: ENG-4387 for billing-side usage attribution and SUP-1987 for a customer support case that motivated smoothing behavior.

review_comments: Asha Patel: Overall looks good, great test coverage. A few nits: please split the very large token_bucket_controller.go into controller + helpers to keep reviewable and add comments on the refill math.
Marina Lopez (author): Split file and added math comments; added an additional unit test for refill edge cases.
Tom Nguyen: Did you consider having guarantees apply to specific instance types? We should discuss mapping guarantees to capacity classes.
Marina Lopez: Good point — added an additional field in fleet_config.proto to optionally scope guarantees to capacity_class. Left global default behavior unchanged.
Ravi Mehta: CI flaked on integration test in the first run; rerun looks clean. Please add a brief note in the changelog about possible transient RejectedRequests during rollout.
Marina Lopez: Added changelog note and a small retry in the integration harness to reduce flakes.
merge_details: Merged via squash by Asha Patel. Commit message: 'dedicated: autoscaler throughput guarantees, burst controls, utilization reporting — implement token-bucket burst controller, add fleet guarantees, export new metrics, console UI behind feature flag'
release_notes: Operators can now configure fleet-level throughput guarantees and token-bucket burst controls for Dedicated capacity. New metrics are available for utilization and burst consumption. Defaults preserve existing behavior; enabling guarantees requires admission checks. See docs/admin/dedicated-autoscaler.md for migration steps.
